subject: ancient Chinese city wall
title: A 600-Year-Old Wall Is Glued With Rice Soup, and a Bulldozer Couldn't Move It

scenes.text: A bulldozer couldn't knock down this wall. The mortar is made with rice.
About 1,500 years ago, Chinese builders started mixing sticky rice soup into their lime mortar.
The rice carbohydrate controls how the lime crystals grow, so the mortar sets tighter and shrugs off water.
Chemists at Zhejiang University tested a 600-year-old Nanjing city wall in 2010. The rice was still in it.
Some rice-mortar tombs and walls have survived earthquakes. One Ming tomb part was so firm a bulldozer could do nothing.
Probably the first composite mortar in history, and it only gets stronger with age.

description:
A bulldozer couldn't knock down this wall, because the mortar is made with rice.
About 1,500 years ago builders in China began mixing sticky rice soup into slaked lime. A 2010 study by Bingjian Zhang at Zhejiang University, published in Accounts of Chemical Research, found that amylopectin from the rice controls the growth of calcium carbonate crystals, giving a denser, water-resistant mortar. The team analysed a 600-year-old Nanjing city wall; rice-lime structures such as tombs, pagodas and city walls have survived earthquakes, and one Ming tomb section resisted a modern bulldozer.
What food would you build a house out of?
first_comment: Restorers are using the same rice recipe today to repair an 800-year-old bridge. Which ancient building trick should we bring back?
